final_message:
I reproduced the bug and fixed it. With the fix, `Test` in the report prints as `{ prop1: "hello"; }`, as in 5.6.

**Reproduction (before the fix)**

The check is `node /tmp/repro/check.js <path-to-typescript.js> /tmp/repro/report_exact.ts`. It exits non-zero unless `type Test = Unwrap<typeof value>` prints as `{ prop1: "hello"; }`. `report_exact.ts` is the report's code verbatim.

| Compiler | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 5.7.2 and this checkout | `{ prop1: Wrapper<"hello">; }`, exit 1 |
| 5.6.3 | `{ prop1: "hello"; }`, exit 0 |
| This checkout, with the report's workaround (assertion on its own line) | `{ prop1: "hello"; }`, exit 0 |

Only the printed type was wrong. `Test["prop1"]` was already `"hello"`, so the checker had the right type and the type printer chose the wrong text. The same bad text appeared in `.d.ts` output and in error messages.

The same fault also produced `z: T[]` with an out-of-scope `T` in the declaration emit of `function g<T>(t: T) { return { z: t as T[] }; }`. Neither 5.6.3 nor this checkout does that; 5.7.2 does.

**Cause**

When the node builder prints a property of a mapped, instantiated, spread or union type, that property symbol reuses the declarations of the property it came from. Since 5.7 (the node type printer extraction, #59282), the printer builds the type from the original property's syntax, here the `as Wrapper<"hello">` assertion. It never checked that the derived symbol has the same type as that declaration, so it printed `Wrapper<"hello">` instead of `"hello"`.

**Fix**

The fix is in `src/compiler/checker.ts`. `serializeTypeForDeclaration` now calls a new helper, `isTypeOfDeclarationSymbol`, before using syntax from a declaration. For a symbol that isn't the declaration's own, the helper requires its type to equal the declaration's symbol type, ignoring `undefined`. If it doesn't match, the printer falls back to printing the symbol's actual type.

**Tests**

- I added `tests/cases/compiler/typeAssertionPropertyInDerivedTypes.ts` with baselines. It covers the report's mapped-type case, a spread of it, the generic `T[]` case, and a plain object whose written types are still kept. On 5.7.2 its `.d.ts` shows the wrong output.
- One existing baseline changed, `mappedTypeRecursiveInference.types`. `location: Location` is now expanded to the reverse-mapped object type, which is what 5.6.3 prints and what the type actually is.
- `npx hereby runtests-parallel --light=false --lint=false` was run on an earlier, stricter version of the guard. It gave 96830 passing and 14 failing. Ten were baseline differences, now down to the one above after I loosened the guard. Four were timeouts because the machine was overloaded, and they pass when run alone.
- I did not re-run the whole suite after loosening the guard. I re-ran the ten affected tests, the four timed-out ones and the new test, and they all pass.
- `eslint` is clean on `checker.ts`. I couldn't run `dprint` because its plugin download is blocked by the proxy.
